topic: Higher Order Derivatives: Understanding Rates of Change of Rates

sections.title: Prerequisite Review: The Velocity of Motion
lecture_lines: The derivative f'(x) represents the instantaneous rate of change.
animations: Display formula f'(x) and highlight it. (Color: #FFFFFF)
Show a position-time graph as a curve. (Color: #FFFF00)

sections.title: Defining the Second Derivative
lecture_lines: The second derivative f''(x) is the derivative of f'(x).
It measures acceleration, or how velocity changes.
Graphically, it determines the curve's concavity.
animations: Display f'(x) and f''(x) notation clearly using the for rate of change visualization. (Color: #00FFFF)
Plot acceleration as a function of time using the to represent input. (Color: #FF9900)
Animate concavity changing on f(x) with the moving along the curve. (Color: #FF0000)

sections.title: Visualizing Concavity
lecture_lines: If f''(x) > 0, the curve is concave up.
If f''(x) < 0, the curve is concave down.
Concavity visually describes the curve's bend.
animations: Draw concave up parabola in green. (Color: #00FF00)
Draw concave down parabola in blue. (Color: #0000FF)
Label inflection point with white circle. (Color: #FFFFFF)

sections.title: Generalizing to Higher Orders (n-th derivative)
lecture_lines: We can continue the derivative process further.
Higher derivatives offer refined information about smoothness.
animations: Show f(x) and its derivative f'(x). (Color: #FFFFFF)

sections.title: Summary & Quick Check
lecture_lines: Higher derivatives reveal how functions evolve.
animations: Display summary table for all derivatives. (Color: #FFFFFF)
Apply pulse effect to all labels. (Color: #00FFFF)
